summary: When a plain animal is shechted, the foreleg, the cheeks and the stomach are given to the Kohen (the matanos). This applies everywhere and always, but not to korbanos, as the pasuk teaches.

chunks.en: The foreleg, the cheeks, and the stomach apply
chunks.explain: These parts of a shechted animal are gifts for the Kohen.
chunks.st: The mitzva to give the foreleg, the jaw, and the maw of slaughtered animals to the priests, known as the gifts of the priesthood, applies both

chunks.en: in Eretz Yisrael and outside Eretz Yisrael,

chunks.en: when the Beis HaMikdash stands and when it does not,
chunks.st: in the presence of the Temple and not in the presence of the Temple, and it applies

chunks.en: with plain animals but not with korbanos.
chunks.st: to non-sacred animals, but not to sacrificial animals.

summary: An animal that had a lasting blemish before it was made holy, once redeemed, is almost like a plain animal. But if it became holy first and got a blemish later, much of its holiness stays even after it is redeemed.

chunks.en: All korbanos that had a lasting blemish

chunks.st: All sacrificial animals in

chunks.st: which a permanent blemish preceded their consecration do not assume inherent sanctity, and only their value is consecrated.

chunks.st: And once they were redeemed, they are obligated in the mitzva of a firstborn, i.e., their offspring are subject to being counted a firstborn, and in the gifts of the priesthood,

chunks.en: to be sheared and to be worked.

summary: When a bechor is mixed up with other animals, some are free from the matanos. A Kohen's or non-Jew's animal is free from the matanos, and the mishnah explains who gives them when meat is bought.

chunks.en: A bechor that got mixed with a hundred animals:
chunks.st: With regard to a blemished firstborn animal, which one may slaughter and eat without being required to give the foreleg, jaw, and maw to the priest, that was intermingled with one hundred non-sacred animals, from which one is required to give those gifts,

chunks.en: when a hundred people shecht all of them,
chunks.st: in a case when one hundred different people slaughter all of them, each slaughtering one animal,

chunks.en: we free all of them.
chunks.st: one exempts them all from giving the gifts, as each could claim that the animal that he slaughtered was the firstborn.

chunks.en: If one person shechts all of them,
chunks.st: If one person slaughtered them all,

chunks.en: we free one of them for him.
chunks.st: one exempts one of the animals for him.
